name: Polyethylene Terephthalate
description: PET is a strong, lightweight, transparent plastic widely used in beverage containers, food packaging, and synthetic fibers.

recyclability.description: PET is 100% recyclable and has established mechanical recycling infrastructure worldwide.

disposalRecommendation: Recycle in dedicated PET/Curbside recycling bins. Ensure the bottle is empty, clean, and caps/labels are removed where required.

environmentalImpact.description: Widely recyclable but slow to degrade natively. Microplastic shedding occurs if landfilled or littered.

name: High-Density Polyethylene
description: HDPE is a versatile, high-density thermoplastic with high strength-to-density ratio, excellent moisture resistance, and chemical stability.

recyclability.description: One of the easiest polymers to recycle into sturdy long-term products such as plastic lumber and pipes.

disposalRecommendation: Rinse thoroughly and place in standard plastic recycling stream.

environmentalImpact.description: Non-toxic, highly durable, low leaching risk, easily re-processed into secondary goods.

name: Polyvinyl Chloride
description: PVC is a durable polymer used in rigid structural applications and flexible tubing. Contains chlorine compounds.

recyclability.description: Difficult to recycle mechanically due to additives and chlorine content. Requires specialized facilities.

disposalRecommendation: Do not burn or place in standard curbside bins. Take to specialized construction material recycling centers.

environmentalImpact.description: Can release hazardous dioxins during thermal incineration if unmanaged.

name: Low-Density Polyethylene
description: LDPE is flexible, lightweight, and tough with high impact strength and moisture protection.

recyclability.description: Recyclable primarily through dedicated store drop-off programs for plastic films.

disposalRecommendation: Bundle soft plastic film and return to supermarket film drop-off bins.

environmentalImpact.description: Lightweight and low energy to produce, but easily winds up as windborne litter if uncollected.

name: Polypropylene
description: PP is a tough, heat-tolerant polymer ideal for reusable food containers, bottle caps, and auto parts.

recyclability.description: Increasingly accepted in curbside programs and remanufactured into automotive components and bins.

disposalRecommendation: Clean food residue and place in municipal plastic recycling.

environmentalImpact.description: Safe, BPA-free, high fatigue resistance allows repeated reuse before recycling.

name: Polystyrene
description: PS exists as solid plastic (clear cutlery) or expanded foam (Styrofoam) providing insulation.

recyclability.description: Expanded foam PS is voluminous, brittle, and rarely accepted in standard curbside collection.

disposalRecommendation: Avoid single-use PS. Dispose in solid waste stream or specialty EPS foam drop-offs.

environmentalImpact.description: Fragments easily into persistent microplastics and leaches styrene monomers under heat.

name: Acrylonitrile Butadiene Styrene
description: ABS is an engineering thermoplastic known for high impact resistance, rigidity, and smooth glossy surface finish.

recyclability.description: 100% recyclable through e-waste shredding and industrial polymer recovery.

disposalRecommendation: Dispose via e-waste recycling stations or electronics take-back events.

environmentalImpact.description: Extremely long-lasting durable polymer. Low hazard when intact in solid state.
